title: Breakout Candidates
brief: Which players have the role, usage or minutes growth to finish well above their auction price this season? For each, it must name the opening behind the breakout (departed teammate, bigger role, year-two or year-three step) and which category signals support it.
summary: Our best breakout buys are players whose role grows because a teammate left: Reaves, Garland, Brandon Miller and Naz Reid. Add to them the year-three forwards Buzelis and Ausar Thompson, and Kel'el Ware at center. They cost 5 to 40 USD and can finish well above that if the minutes and assists show up. Round-one players like Flagg, Tatum and Giannis already have their growth in the price. Most role-up players outside the 144 we draft are waiver watches, not auction bids.

paragraphs.text: Usage is very stable from year to year (0.83), and so are minutes per game (0.78). Most busts and breakouts come from injuries, to the player or to someone ahead of him, and from random shooting seasons. They rarely come from a natural rise in counting stats. So start with role changes: a trade, an injury or a free agency departure that frees up shots and minutes.

The best setup is a team that lost high-usage players and brought in fewer than it lost. That leftover usage has to go to someone. Before you bid, check who else is on the roster. More high-usage stars mean fewer chances for role players, not more.

A player's best breakout chance is the season with the most opening. When the injured star comes back, expect a step back. Some of this season's openings may not last. Hachimura and Strus get more room only while Ingram is out. Isaiah Jackson starts until Konan Niederhäuser returns. Maluach starts while Mark Williams is out. Podziemski's early role depends on Butler and Moody being out. Price these players for a short window, not a full season.

Age and track record set limits. A long-time veteran turning 29 is probably who he is. A player who showed nothing in his first three years is unlikely to jump in year four. For example, Gobert gains minutes without Reid and Randle, but at 34 he is a cheap three-category center for punt FT% teams, not a breakout.

Lakers: LeBron is gone, and Reaves is the classic third-in-line ball handler next to two stars. Players in that spot can jump in value, especially in assist rate, once one star leaves. Before the draft, check his splits from games he played with only Luka. Expect to pay in the mid 30s and stop near 40 USD.

Charlotte lost LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges. Brandon Miller gets more creation and usage. Coby White starts at point guard at 30 to 32 minutes, up from 25. Naz Reid becomes a starter at a career-high 31 to 33 minutes. Knueppel's usage should rise from 22% to about 24 or 25%. Four players will share that usage, so not all of them can break out. Of the four, Knueppel is the one to let others buy, because our room will likely pay more than Josh's 8 USD limit.

Sacramento lost Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan. Sabonis should get more usage and assists, and Keegan Murray and LaVine get more usage and ball handling. Memphis traded Morant. Coward gets 29 to 30+ minutes, and Jerome starts at point guard, though his usage is expected to drop. Boston lost Jaylen Brown. Tatum is now the top option, and Paul George's projected usage rises from 23 to near 26 as the second option.

Minnesota lost Reid and Randle. McDaniels gets more shots, though Kuminga takes some of them, and Gobert must do more. All Minnesota players have a two-game week in our playoff week 20, so do not stretch for them. The Clippers make Garland their top usage option at about 32 minutes, and experts call him a likely top 30 player against a market near 53 to 65. Brooklyn gives Randle about 30% usage and makes Sharpe the starting center after the Claxton trade.

In recent years, big breakouts have shifted toward year two. Players who did not step up in year two are the ones who tend to break out in year three. Young players usually move from a small rookie role to a bigger one by year three. Use this as a baseline, then judge each player on his own situation.

Year-two candidates: Coward is projected to rise from 10.5 to 14.2 shots per game. Murray-Boyles is projected at 25 or more minutes, with usage rising from 15% to about 18%. Dëmin is a projected starter with usage up to about 20 or 21. Flagg is expected to improve in scoring, efficiency and assists, but he already costs a late first-round price. Josh caps him at about 40 USD, so his jump is mostly priced in.

Year-three candidates: Buzelis is projected for about 32 minutes, with more usage and ball handling under Splitter. Experts agree he is a top 50 player, and anything under 20 USD is a buy. Ware is projected for 26 to 30 minutes after 22, with top 40 upside at 30 minutes, and he cost only 5 USD here last season. Ausar Thompson should get more minutes and on-ball usage, including some of Tobias Harris's old usage. Plan on about 15 to 20 USD for him.

In category leagues, breakouts come from three signals: efficiency at volume, a higher free throw attempt rate and a higher assist rate. Watch for the last two even in players who are not point guards. A jump from about 4 to 6.5 or 7 free throw attempts per game can move a player from around 25th to around 5th. Our player data does not list free throw attempt rates, so track them from box scores in the first two weeks.

Assist checks for October: Reaves rising next to Luka, Sabonis near 6, White at 5 to 6, Ausar Thompson at about 4, and Podziemski while Butler is out. Efficiency-at-volume checks: Miller's FG% is projected at 43% in his bigger creation role. Reid shoots about 46% on about 13 shots. Dëmin needs to climb from 39.9%. Knueppel's FG% has to hold without LaMelo Ball. If assists rise and FG% holds, keep the player. If usage rises but FG% falls, he only fits a punt FG% team.

Small gains add up. A few points better from three, a bit more usage, an extra assist and more minutes can lift a player into the top 50. A good per-game rank earned in limited minutes points to upside once the role grows. Apply this to backups who are moving into starting jobs, such as Sharpe (from about 19 minutes), Missi (from 19.6 minutes) and Reid.

Experts disagree on whether to pay for year-two jumps. One side says usage and minutes are very stable, and that breakouts mostly come from injuries and random shooting rather than growth. The other side says to expect year-two players to jump, and that young players gain usage every year. For our auction, pay full price only for a role change you can see on the depth chart. For a pure year-two or year-three bet, pay only what still works if the jump does not come.

On individual players: some experts expect Naz Reid to finish top 50, while others see no upside beyond his tier. A bid of 10 to 15 USD works either way. Brandon Miller has top 30 upside, but improvement is not guaranteed, so stay within 20 to 26 USD.

Middle rounds: Reaves in the mid 30s (stop near 40 USD), Garland at 20 to 25, Miller at 20 to 26, Buzelis under 20, Ausar Thompson at 15 to 20, White at 13 to 18, Reid at 10 to 15 and George in the low to mid teens. These are the players with both a clear opening and room above their price.

End game: Ware at about 5, Coward at about 6, Sharpe up to 10, Murray-Boyles up to 9, Podziemski near Yahoo's price, and Maluach and Dëmin at 1 to 3. Keegan Murray, LaVine and Collins work as 1 to 5 USD fills. Ingram is a few-dollar IL stash. Do not pay ESPN prices for Podziemski or Jerome.

After the draft, use the 6 weekly adds on minutes, not names. Larsson, Scheierman, Kuzma, Strus, Tyson, Walter, McCain and Sasser only matter if their early minutes show up. Handcuffs move fast on FAB: Beringer if Gobert sits, Reed if Duren sits. An IL slot can hold Konan Niederhäuser for the fantasy playoffs.
